acceptanceCriteria: A descendant that keeps a subprocess's output open still fails the call within a bounded time, and the existing held-pipe tests keep passing.

A doccompiler, taskman, liveverify mutation or work executable binding subprocess that exits 0 while its output reader is starved for several seconds returns its output instead of a WaitDelay failure.
Each changed bound states that it detects a held pipe and is not a latency budget.
body: V1-0390 raised the Git pipe-drain bound in contextindex and gokernel from one second to one minute. The same one-second os/exec WaitDelay remains in internal/doccompiler/process_{unix,other,windows}.go, internal/taskman/process_unix.go, internal/liveverify/mutate/process_{unix,other}.go and cmd/corvint/work_executable_binding.go:287. os/exec starts the WaitDelay timer when the process exits, so a successful subprocess fails with exec: WaitDelay expired before I/O complete whenever the goroutine copying its output is not scheduled within one second. That was observed for Git calls on a host with full swap and load above 400. The groupreap adoption in V1-0373 kills a leftover group before Wait, which closes held pipes, but does not help a starved reader. work_executable_binding has tests that depend on the value.
title: One-second pipe-drain bounds outside Git acquisition fail successful subprocesses on a loaded host
